Instruments

The vessels of the voyage

Each instrument is a different boat for the same journey. Here are the vessels that carry the music of Colibrí — the Instrumentarium.

Strings

Melody & harmony

  • Mandolin

    Eastman PCH-M104-GB

    A-style mandolin

    This little instrument makes a delightful sound reminiscent of the twittering of birds. It is one of the most versatile members of the Instrumentarium, and I use it both for accompaniment and to play soli* over the backing tracks.

    *That is, not just one solo, but more than one.

  • Classical Guitar

    Córdoba C5

    Nylon-string classical guitar

    This instrument has a warmer, sweeter sound than my other guitars, which makes it ideal for ballads and laid-back songs.

    However, this guitar has a lively side, too! I often play it in a supporting role with strumming or fingerpicking.

    It can be seen in live performances by advance request only. It is a delicate instrument, and special packing arrangements must be made to ensure its safe arrival at the venue.

  • Acoustic Guitar

    Yamaha EF-31

    Dreadnought steel-string acoustic-electric guitar

    This faithful member of the Instrumentarium has a pleasant, woody sound that works well in many different styles of music.

    You will usually hear it strumming in the background, but it has a very pleasing sound when played through certain amplifiers.

    The signature is quite faded due to play, but this guitar was signed by Mr. Tommy Emmanuel, C.G.P. (“Certified Guitar Player”). I got to hear him play live in Providence!

Percussion

Rhythm & pulse

  • Maracas

    Latin Percussion · LP281

    Matched pair

    These make a commanding, bright sound when shaken. I have softened their volume by wrapping them in cloth napkins. Maracas often act as the glue for the rest of the percussion ensemble, keeping steady time while the other instruments provide syncopation.

    They come in a matched set; one is voiced low, the other is voiced high.

  • Claves

    Latin Percussion · LP261

    Matched hardwood set

    This is a matched set of hardwood claves. They are an essential member of Latin percussion ensembles because they lock down the groove with their high-pitched bark.

  • Cowbell

    Latin Percussion · LP229

    This cowbell has a rich, resonant sound with an unmistakable metallic edge. In these recordings, I am playing it with a drumstick by Vic Firth (5A model).

  • Bongo Cajón

    Meinl

    Two-chamber bongo cajón

    As you can see in the reverse picture, this instrument has two chambers. The smaller chamber makes a higher pitched sound than the larger one. It has a crisp, woody sound that lives somewhere between a cajón and traditional bongos.

    This type of bongo cajón might be available somewhere, but it comes as a kit that you get to build and customize yourself!

  • Güiro

    Maker currently unknown

    This delightful instrument came to me with the marker drawings on it already. I use the small wooden stick in different ways to vary the pitch and timbre of the sound.

  • Tambourine

    Remo · Fiberskyn head

    Description to come.
